bio: Wright's Historical Sketches of Plymouth (1873) says the Van Loons came to Plymouth from Esopus in 1794, three brothers of Low Dutch origin, Abraham ('Brom'), Mathias and Nicholas, all on the 1796 assessment list, and 'a family of hard workers' ([R4-S1]). Matthias Vanloon is on the 1796 Plymouth taxables list in Pearce's Annals ([R4-S2]). Bradsby names Mathias Van Loon, with Thomas Lamoreaux and others, as one of the 'settlers in the other century' of Jackson Township, the hill country west of Shawnee mountain where the Lamoreuxs settled ([R4-S3]). He married Temperance Lamoreaux (1778-1855), daughter of Ensign Thomas Lamoreaux, and they had eight children (round 2, from Thomas Lamoreaux's will and Giles & Franklin). His nephew Stephen Van Loon (Abraham's eldest son) married her sister Hannah, so uncle and nephew married sisters.
